data.description:
## Description

What: Create tests/runners/test-runner-equivalence.sh. For each corpus case, run each in-scope engine via its manifest-declared invocation method (suite-engine direct file args; bash-runner via test-batched.sh --filter), apply the per-harness verdict-extraction adapter to normalize engine outcomes (including interrupted/timeout) to the canonical {pass,fail,skip} vocabulary while rejecting unknown tokens loudly, and assert each in-scope engine produces the oracle verdict. Out-of-scope cases (per the case's harnesses annotation) report 'out of scope' rather than running. Use mktemp for all intermediate state, and wire the test into validate.sh --ci. Why: This is the core gate that operationalizes the single-oracle model. Scope IN: per-case per-engine invocation via the manifest, adapter normalization including timeout/interrupted mapping and loud unknown-token rejection, oracle-verdict assertion, scope-annotation handling, mktemp intermediate state, validate.sh --ci wiring. Scope OUT: parallel invocation and the wall-clock budget assertion + pre-commit fast-subset (sc-3 performance clause -> draft-4); the pre-commit hook (sc-4); the classification-semantics doc-presence assertion (sc-5).

## Done Definitions

- For each in-scope corpus case, the test invokes each in-scope engine via its manifest-declared method and asserts the adapter-normalized verdict equals the oracle verdict ← Satisfies: sc-3
- The verdict-extraction adapter maps interrupted/timeout engine outcomes to the canonical {pass,fail,skip} vocabulary and rejects an unknown engine-output token with a loud non-zero failure ← Satisfies: sc-3
- A case out of scope for an engine (per its harnesses annotation) reports 'out of scope' for that engine instead of asserting a verdict ← Satisfies: sc-3
- All intermediate state is created via mktemp and the test runs as part of validate.sh --ci ← Satisfies: sc-3
- An integration test exercises the equivalence test in a configuration-isolated environment (HOME set to an empty directory, no pre-existing worktrees, no global git config, no environment variables pre-set from the developer's machine) and the test passes ← Satisfies: sc-3

## Considerations

- [Boundary] tests/runners/** and the new test-runner-equivalence.sh must be in the plugin-boundary allowlist; set the executable bit on test-runner-equivalence.sh.
- [Correctness] The adapter must distinguish a genuine fail from a timeout/interrupted outcome to avoid masking drift.
- [Shared-Setup] The configuration-isolated environment setup (empty HOME, no global git config, no pre-existing worktrees, no pre-set developer environment variables) is shared with draft-6. Extract it into a single shared helper under tests/lib/ so both draft-3's integration test and draft-6's pre-commit hook integration test consume one implementation — otherwise the hook and the CI test isolate differently, violating the 'identical script' guarantee.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a runner-contract maintainer, I want an equivalence test that runs each in-scope engine per corpus case and asserts it produces the oracle verdict, so that engine drift is caught at authoring time rather than post-merge.
